notes: Three real bullets and twelve of fishing testimonial. Everything under '== Fishing Testimonials ==' (bullets 4 to 15) is one player after another naming a rod-and-bait pair that worked; none of it is an instruction, so none of it is a step -- the west and north shores and the G-9 watercraft dock come out of it only as a note on where to stand. The loop is the point of this quest and the ladder cannot express it: every Delectable Orobon drops exactly one Delectable Orobon Steak, but the cut is rolled at random out of five and only the liver satisfies Nestroh, so the player fishes, trades, is rejected, and fishes again. Holding a steak is genuinely observable and genuinely means 'go back to Nestroh', which is the right mark even though it will often be wrong about being finished; nothing in a packet distinguishes a liver cut from a tail cut before he tries it. The page never names the five cuts as items -- only as the words tail, stomach, cheeks, back and liver -- so the one name it does give, Delectable Orobon Steak, is the one recorded. 'Quest Reqs: A fishing rod' has no slot in the schema and the testimonials list a dozen rods that all work, so picking one to put in items would be inventing an exclusion the page does not make; it stays a note. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the addon's nine regions and gates nothing.

steps.note: near Bivouac #3

fished up, not walked into: you need a rod and bait, and the orobon becomes a monster on the hook. One guaranteed steak per kill. The testimonials put the fish on the west and north shores of the island and at the watercraft dock in the north-east corner of (G-9); no grid is recorded because none of that is an instruction.
only a liver cut sates him; every other cut is rejected and you go back to step 2. He will happily take a cut he has already tried, so repeats are expected.

notes:
Bullets 1 and 2 are the same conversation with the same NPC -- the first attempt opens the WRONG quest (Chocobo on the Loose!) and you have to speak twice more and answer 'Nope, never!' to land on this one -- so they are one step and one marker. The interesting target is the chocobo itself, which the page names only as 'the chocobo standing next to Osker'. 'Chocobo' is on the resolver's known-ambiguous list, so recording it keeps the rung but will probably never carry a marker; the alternative, pointing at Osker, would be marking a bystander the sentence merely uses as a landmark, which is exactly the failure this rebuild exists to avoid. That step is 'medium' for it. The Chocobo license is the header's Reward, so by rule it is not evidence for the feeding step even though bullet 5 hands it over there -- the only thing observable in this quest is holding the grass, which is why it sits on the obtain step. Counts do not survive contact with the page either: the header asks for four, but the walkthrough says six feeding attempts of which the first two fail for free, so four is what is actually consumed and four is what is recorded. Bullet 6 is advice about the NEXT quest (no zoning needed, but buy the Map of the Jeuno area first) and is not a step. Feeding is capped at one attempt per real-life minute, clocked from :00 rather than from your last attempt, which nothing in the packets reports.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: so this step carries no zone of its own.
  step 3: 'chocobo' is a known-ambiguous name and may never resolve to a live entity.

The Chocobo license arrives here but it is the header's Reward, not evidence.

notes: The walkthrough jumps straight from 'travel to the Cloister of Tremors' to 'Defeat Titan Prime' and never says how you get into the battlefield -- but the header Description does ('Ring the tuning fork of earth upon the protocrystal in the Quicksand Caves. A path will open to the trial that awaits'), and Notes [6] says 'enter the Protocrystal normally'. So the trade step is recorded, attributed to bullet 3 which presupposes it, and marked medium; without it the ladder would hand the player a tuning fork and then never use it, which is the header field going unused that the guide warns is a sign of a truncated walkthrough. The page only ever writes 'the protocrystal', never 'Earth Protocrystal', so that is the name recorded. Bullet 2 is three legs of a journey in one sentence and is split at the zone lines: the cave mouth at (J-7) is in Eastern Altepa Desert, the hidden entrance at (E-10) is inside Quicksand Caves, and each step keeps the grid of the zone it actually happens in rather than inheriting its destination's. All seven bullets of the 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section are limits and advice -- party size, per-member forks, the 30 minute clock, one reward at a time, the once-per-Earth-day repeat, the Trial-Size Mini Fork of Earth shortcut, and the warning to hold the whisper for The Moonlit Path -- and not one of them is a step. The Trial-Size route through Ferrol is a different quest's key item and deliberately not modelled here. The Whisper of tremors is evidence on the fight and the requirement for the hand-in, which is why the last step can be held indefinitely.

a hidden entrance; the page's map shows the hidden tunnels, falls and traps -- do not drop into the wrong area. Home point at Quicksand Caves #2 if you can, and the Unity 125 warp lands about a minute's run from it.

she offers a choice of rewards including the pact with Titan, one at a time. Do NOT hand in if you still need the whisper for The Moonlit Path. Repeats wait for the next Earth day, which nothing observable reports.

notes: A clean eleven-bullet page that reads almost straight through. Two judgement calls. First, bullets 5 and 6 are kept apart rather than merged: examining an Iron Grille and trading a Dorter Key to one are different actions on the same object and the page is emphatic about the order -- a key traded to an empty cell is simply gone -- so collapsing them would hide the one warning that costs the player something. They share the object and the zone, so they are one marker either way. The grilles sit in two separate outdoor areas of the second floor, (E-7) and (G-9), and no single grid is true of the step, so both live in the note and the grid is null. Second, nothing observable counts prisoners: the Poet god's key only arrives after the third cutscene, so the whole freeing loop is one step whose evidence is that key, and a player two-thirds done looks identical to one who has just started. Bullets 8 and 9 are one step on the Collapsing Floor -- check it for a cutscene, check it again to enter -- exactly the double-examine pattern. The Poet god's key is recorded as what you must hold to enter, which the page implies rather than states: bullet 11 says a loss sends you back to the Mithran Bivouac to re-obtain it. That loss-recovery return is a note, but the OTHER conditional in bullet 11 is a real place you have to go, so the reward pickup at the Bivouac is an optional last step -- it only happens if you won while already carrying a Hi-Reraiser. Fame 'Wings of the Goddess' is an expansion name, not one of the nine regions, and gates nothing.

the outdoor areas of the castle's second floor, of which there are two, at (E-7) and (G-9) -- no single grid is true of the step. Click grilles until the message says you sense someone on the other side.

at the top of the castle; the climb is the same as present-day Castle Oztroja -- see the Yagudo crest segment of Whence Blows the Wind -- except that no Yagudo name password is needed here. Check it once for a cutscene, again to enter the battlefield.

the elementals cast Aeroga, Aeroga II, Silence and Gravity; Tzee Xicu's Kamitachi is a full dispel with high damage and a hate reset. Only Tzee Xicu has to die. Lose and you go back to the Mithran Bivouac for another Poet god's key.
only if you won while already carrying a Hi-Reraiser -- then the reward is collected here instead of handed over at the end of the fight.

notes: The header's giver, Robel-Akbel, does not appear anywhere in the walkthrough. Bullet 1 says the quest opens on a cutscene when you ZONE INTO Windurst Waters (S) after finishing When One Man Is Not Enough, and the NPC who actually takes the hand-in twelve bullets later is Dhea Prandoleh. Unlike Carbuncle Debacle, where the header's cutscene giver could be swapped for a real standing object, there is nothing here to move the marker to -- the trigger is the zone line itself -- so start.npc keeps Robel-Akbel as a fallback that at least points at the right zone, step 1 is the zone entry, and both flags are set. Bullet 1's sub-bullet and bullet 2's second sub-bullet are the page's own '(Optional)': the first is a real second NPC and is recorded as an optional step, the second is Mham Lahrih repeating himself and is only a note, because a second step on an NPC you are already standing in front of buys nothing. Bullets 3 and 4 are kept apart even though they are the same Abandoned Mineshaft: the first click grants the Signal firecracker and the second spends it, so splitting them is what lets the key item be evidence on one step and a requirement on the next. Bullets 5 to 10 are all one fight. The Quadav and the Gigas are named only by race, never individually, so no mobs are recorded for them -- inventing entries would be exactly the guessing this rebuild avoids -- and Romaa Mihgo and the Wildcat Volunteers are allies, not targets. Bullet 11 is a pointer to the Discussion page and bullet 12 sits under a '== Wrap up ==' heading but is a plain hand-in. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is one line redirecting mission players to In the Name of the Father and holds no steps.

the second click enters Ghoyu's Reverie. Up to six players, each needing the firecracker or a previous clear, and the party leader must be holding one.

notes: Bullet 2 is a whole top-level bullet of Windower troubleshooting -- unload FastCS and drop to 30 fps or the cutscene freezes -- and is not a step at all. This is the Divine Might lesson repeating itself, and a verb-scanner would have made an action out of it. Everything else reads straight. 'Level: 90+ Geomancer' is both gates, so 90 and GEO; bullet 1's sub-bullet makes it explicit that only the opening conversation needs the job and anything can finish the quest, which the runtime gets for free because prerequisites are only evaluated for quests you have not started. Bullets 4 and 5 are the same Overgrown Grave clicked twice, once for a cutscene and once to spawn the NM, so they are one step and one marker; bullet 6 is a THIRD click on the same grave, and it stays a separate step because the page really does put a fight in between -- this is the case the guide's 'unless the page really does' clause exists for. Nothing observable comes out of the fight, so its evidence is null rather than reaching for something. The bell is granted at Nhili Uvolep and taken back by Sylvie at the end, which is why it is evidence on one step and a requirement on the other; players who arrive without it get Bayld instead, once ever. Fame 'Seekers of Adoulin' is an expansion name, not one of the nine regions.

Sverdhried Hillock, Waypoint #7. If you still hold the Trial Wand, or she offers Geomancerrific instead, talk to her twice. Bullet 2 is the page's Windower warning about this cutscene -- unload FastCS and set FrameRateDivisor 2 first -- not a step. Turning up later without the bell earns Bayld instead, once only.

examine once for a cutscene, again to spawn the NM. Cirdas Caverns - Augural Conveyor is the fastest warp, otherwise Yorcia Weald Frontier Station; a Colonization Reive may be in the way and have to be cleared first.

about 70k HP, a Gravitation elemental of earth and darkness with very high physical damage reduction. Sleepga 2, AOE Drain and Aspir, Entomb (earth damage, Slow, Petrify, hate reset) and Tenebral Crush (darkness damage, Defense Down). Formless Strikes does not work on it; Repose and Lullaby do.
